evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the system constraint that prevents multiple operators from having simultaneous command control, which is the root condition for the exception flow where a new user attempts to take control.

evidence_cards.content: The Operator User Class is authorized to change system mode.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Confirms that the primary actor has the specific privilege required to trigger the command control conflict scenario.

evidence_cards.content: The System Administrator User Class is also authorized to change system mode.

source_locations.location: Table under Section 2.3, Row 'System Administrator', Column 'Functions'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a secondary actor who could potentially initiate a command control takeover or conflict, relevant to the exception flow logic.

evidence_cards.content: If command control is enabled by another user, and the logging in user is of higher security, the logging in user shall be requested to accept or deny command control.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the system response (request to accept/deny) when a higher-security user attempts to log in while command control is active, which constitutes an exception flow condition.

evidence_cards.content: If another user is logged in with command control and the new user takes command control, the other user is notified.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the notification outcome for the displaced user when a takeover occurs, serving as part of the exception handling logic.

evidence_cards.content: At any point in an opening or closing sequence, the sequence shall be halted if a device fails to report completion of the current sequence step within the response time window allotted for the step.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific exception trigger (timeout) that interrupts the main flow of a mode change sequence.

evidence_cards.content: At any point in an opening or closing sequence, the sequence shall be halted if the status of a closure device changes to 'unknown' or 'closed' (if previously opened) or 'unknown' or 'open' (if previously closed) without an operator-initiated command.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines exception triggers based on unauthorized state changes during the sequence.

evidence_cards.content: At any point in an opening sequence, the sequence shall be halted if the status of a closure device for the opposite direction of travel changes to 'unknown' or 'open'.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a safety-related exception trigger specific to opening sequences.

evidence_cards.content: To resume an opening or closing sequence after a halt has occurred, the operator shall be able to issue a command to resume if the offending device status can be corrected within a configurable time period as defined in the database and in non-volatile memory.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the recovery path and constraints (configurable time period) for resuming the sequence after an exception.

evidence_cards.content: Unknown, or improper closure device status anywhere in the system, will immediately terminate a 'device opening' command. Improper device status 'may' terminate a device closing command, or sequence.

source_locations.location: Section F.10, item 5 under 'Characteristics Bearing on Security'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an exception flow triggered by uncertain or improper device status during command execution — directly relevant to error handling paths when changing system mode (which may involve device state changes). It specifies termination behavior for opening commands and conditional termination for closing commands, which constitutes concrete exception response logic.
